title: Context Relay Broker: lightweight telemetry handoff for async runtimes
creator: Miles Chen
description:
Problem: Our SDKs currently lose or bloat trace/context metadata when crossing async boundaries (worker threads, background job queues, language fiber switches). This leads to broken trace continuity in distributed traces and inflated headers in high-throughput paths.

Proposal: Implement a small, language-agnostic Context Relay Broker (CRB) embedded in SDK runtimes and middleware. The CRB provides: a compact context token (64-bit fingerprint + optional small sample flag), a tiny binary-compat TTL, and a handshake for trusted process-to-process handoff. It intentionally avoids full baggage propagation to keep headers small and minimizes allocations during hot paths. CRB will interoperate with existing OTEL traces and our internal trace enrichment pipeline via a translation layer in the agent.

Scope: SDK changes for Node, Python, and Go; middleware adapters for HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, and job queue clients (Redis/Sidekiq/RQ/Kafka producers); runtime tests, benchmarks, and a staged canary rollout behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end distributed traces remain stitched across async boundaries for 99.9% of sampled requests in integration test harness
Header size increase under 32 bytes for common request paths (no baggage), and no more than 10% additional CPU on p95 for SDK hot-paths
CRB supports fallbacks: when remote side is CRB-unaware, tracing degrades gracefully without duplication or infinite sampling loops
Interoperability test with OTEL: traces generated with OTEL SDKs are correlated with CRB tokens in our collector in >98% cases
Library version gated rollout with feature-flag canary, ability to opt-out per-customer or per-route
Documentation and migration guide for customers and internal teams published in Confluence and SDK CHANGELOGs
design_decisions: Compact token: 64-bit trace fingerprint (base64) + 1 byte flags rather than full-w3c baggage to reduce header size
Hop TTL: include a 1-byte hop counter to prevent long-lived tokens; receiver decrements and drops when zero
Sampling alignment: token carries a sampling hint bit; collector reconciles with OTEL sampling to avoid double-counting
Trust model: CRB accepts tokens only from trusted origins (signed HMAC optional in private deployments), default: unsigned in hosted mode to avoid crypto overhead
No baggage: heavy key/value baggage will not be encoded; recommend using logs/attributes to ship extra metadata
Backward compatibility: if an incoming request has W3C traceparent, CRB will map token to parent trace ID at edge; do not override existing traceparent unless configured
implementation_plan: 1) Spec document: CRB wire token format, handshake, and fallback semantics (ENG-20577-spec)
2) SDK changes: implement CRB encoder/decoder, async boundary hooks, and low-allocation fast-paths for Node/Python/Go
3) Middleware adapters: HTTP/gRPC/WS wrappers to inject/extract token; job queue instrumentations for producer/consumer
4) Collector bridge: implement translation to OTEL attributes and sample reconciliation in telemetry ingestion (collector PR refs will be added)
5) Performance harness: microbenchmarks and flame graphs; include CI gate for p50/p95 overhead vs baseline
6) Docs & example apps: quickstart, migration guide, and rollout checklist
7) PRs: create feature branches per SDK repo; link GH PRs in comments when opened
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged release in SDKs (off by default)
Canary: enable CRB for internal services and 2% of hosted traffic for 7 days; monitor trace continuity and CPU/latency regressions
Stage 2: expand to 20% if metrics stable; run targeted integration tests with major partners
Stage 3: opt-in by default in next minor SDK release after 30-day observation, with per-customer opt-out available for Private deployments
Rollback: server-side collector accepts both old and new tokens; rollback client SDK flag to disable immediately if regressions detected
test_plan: Unit tests for encoder/decoder edge cases (expired hop count, malformed tokens, mixed OTEL headers)
Integration harness: weave worker threads, background jobs, and HTTP/gRPC flows to assert trace continuity
Load test: 2000rps synthetic traffic with realistic workloads to measure header overhead and CPU impact
A/B canary validation: compare trace completion rates and end-to-end latency between control and CRB groups
Long-running soak (48h) on staging to surface memory leaks in SDK hooks
Security fuzzing of token parsing and handshake code paths
open_questions: Do we require HMAC signing of tokens in Dedicated/Private deployments by default or make it opt-in?
Should the CRB token replace or be an adjunct to w3c traceparent in all SDKs, or only when traceparent missing?
How to version token format and plan migration path for older SDKs?
Which job queue libraries get priority instrumentation (Sidekiq, Celery, Kafka, Redis Streams)?
What telemetry dashboards will show CRB adoption and health (new panels or extend existing tracing dashboards)?
